To: d.kerrigan@northmail.example
Replying to: m01
Cc: none
Subject: Re: Blister packs for my mother - new patient

Dear Mr. Kerrigan,

Thank you for contacting Erindale Park Pharmacy. I'm sorry to hear about your mother's fall and hospital stay. We would be very happy to look after Mrs. Kerrigan, and I'll do my best to have everything in place for her return home. Here are answers to your questions.

1. Blister packs and cost
Yes, we prepare weekly blister packs with up to four dose times a day (morning, noon, evening and bedtime). There is no charge for the packaging. Your mother will pay only the regular dispensing fees, and at 81 most of her medications should be covered by the Ontario Drug Benefit program.

2. Delivery or pickup
We deliver free within 8 km, and her building on Mississauga Valley Blvd is well within that. Our regular deliveries are on Tuesdays and Fridays between 2 and 6 pm. For the first packs we can hold them for pickup on Saturday, or we can drop them off at her condo on Saturday before 1 pm, whichever is easier for you.

3. Moving her prescriptions
You don't need to do anything with her current pharmacy. We contact them directly and arrange the transfer. We just need the pharmacy's name and address on Dundas and your mother's OHIP number. If you'd prefer not to send her OHIP number by email, please call me with it.

4. Going over her new medications
I would be glad to review her medication list with you, and evenings work well for me. Before we can discuss her medications with you, though, we need your mother's permission. We record this with a signed Family Communication Consent form. It's a simple one-page form, and it protects her privacy by making sure her health information is shared only with the people she chooses. Once she signs it, you can call us about her medications at any time. She can sign it when the first packs are picked up, or our driver can bring it with the Saturday delivery and return it to us.

I would also like to offer your mother a MedsCheck. This is a free 20-minute review with a pharmacist, which we recommend after a hospital stay, especially when there are new medications. Since she has just come home after a fall, I'm happy to do it at her home during her first week. I could come on Monday or Tuesday evening after 6 pm, and you'd be very welcome to be there.

Timing
We need about 48 hours after we receive all of her prescriptions, which means both the hospital discharge prescriptions and the transferred ones. If you could ask the discharge team to fax her prescriptions to us early on Thursday morning (our fax number is [FAX NUMBER]), we should have her first packs ready on Saturday.

This means the packs won't be ready on the day she is discharged. Could you please confirm with the discharge team that she will go home with enough medication to last until Saturday? It would also help to arrange for someone to help her with every dose until then, since she has been mixing up her pills and several of them are new. If there is any problem with the interim supply, please let me know and we will work something out.

You can reach me directly at 905-555-0148 ext. 2. I am in the store Monday to Friday, 9 am to 6 pm. If it's easier, reply to this email with a good evening time and I'll call you at 647-555-0193.

We look forward to caring for your mother.

Kind regards,

Rania Haddad
Pharmacist
Erindale Park Pharmacy
905-555-0148 ext. 2

reasons: It does not ask Douglas to confirm arrangements for help with every dose with the discharge team until Saturday pickup or delivery.
